GREEN’S OPEN PROBLEM 51 AT DENSITY ONE HALF:
BOUNDED CODIMENSION IN BINARY SUMSETS
JENSEN KOHLMEYER AND LIAM KRUER
ABSTRACT. We prove that if 𝐴 ⊆ F𝑛
2 has density at least 1/2 − 𝜀, where 0 ≤ 𝜀 ≤ 1/4, then 𝐴 + 𝐴 contains a
linear subspace of codimension at most 1+256𝑒 𝑛𝜀2. Consequently, density at least 1/2−𝑘/√𝑛 guarantees
a subspace of codimension at most ⌈1 + 256𝑒𝑘 2⌉ for all sufficiently large 𝑛. This answers the one-half-
density question recorded under Green’s Problem 51, and Question 5.1 of Sanders. The proof combines an
elementary variance estimate for ternary separators of the Boolean cube, averaging over random coordinate
faces, and polynomial interpolation on a minimal covering obstruction. A complete Lean 4 formalization
of the specified Formal Conjectures target accompanies the paper.

The argument has two parts. First, for every nonempty subset 𝐷 of the missing sums 𝐺 \ ( 𝐴 +
𝐴), we find a linear functional that vanishes on at most a 256𝜀2 fraction of 𝐷. To do this, we lift a
difference of indicators to a ternary function on a cube whose coordinates are indexed by 𝐷. A separator
estimate and an average over random faces force a nonzero Walsh coefficient of small degree. That
coefficient identifies the required functional. Second, polynomial interpolation bounds the size of a
minimal obstruction to covering the missing sums by complements of kernels. Combining this bound
with repeated application of the first part removes the logarithmic loss that a direct greedy argument on
the whole set would incur.
All vector spaces and linear functionals in the combinatorial argument are over F2. Expectations on
finite sets use the uniform probability measure unless another distribution is specified. The analytic
statements use real-valued functions. Sections 2–6 give a self-contained proof; Section 7 describes the
accompanying formalization.
